statement: Let V = {1,...,n}. For each index i with 0 <= i < len(connections), let a_i = connections[i][0], b_i = connections[i][1], and c_i = connections[i][2]. A subset S of the index set {0,...,len(connections)-1} is feasible if, for every pair of cities u,v in V, there is a walk using only selected connections: there exist m >= 0 and vertices p_0,...,p_m such that p_0 = u, p_m = v, and for each j = 1,...,m there is an index t_j in S such that the unordered pair {p_{j-1}, p_j} equals {a_{t_j}, b_{t_j}}. For such S, let Cost(S) = sum over i in S of c_i. The function returns a result r and: if some feasible S exists, then r is the minimum of Cost(S) over all feasible S, meaning there is a feasible S0 with Cost(S0) = r and r <= Cost(T) for every feasible T; if no feasible S exists, then r = -1.
preconditions: n and connections satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4; 1 <= len(connections) <= 10^4; for every i with 0 <= i < len(connections), len(connections[i]) = 3, 1 <= connections[i][0] <= n, 1 <= connections[i][1] <= n, connections[i][0] != connections[i][1], and 0 <= connections[i][2] <= 10^5. All quantities fit in 64-bit integers.

statement: There exists an integer r such that minimum_cost n connections evaluates to Result.ok r. The function does not fail, panic, overflow, or access out of bounds.
preconditions: n and connections satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4; 1 <= len(connections) <= 10^4; for every i with 0 <= i < len(connections), len(connections[i]) = 3, 1 <= connections[i][0] <= n, 1 <= connections[i][1] <= n, connections[i][0] != connections[i][1], and 0 <= connections[i][2] <= 10^5. All quantities fit in 64-bit integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if no subset S of the connection indices connects all cities in {1,...,n}; here a subset connects all cities when every pair of cities can be joined by a path whose edges are exactly the connections with indices in S, and the empty subset is allowed.

statement: Whenever both calls return results r and r_prime, we have r = r_prime.
preconditions: Both (n, connections) and (n, connections_prime) satisfy the problem constraints, and connections_prime is any permutation of the entries of connections; equivalently, connections_prime has the same length and the same multiset of triples as connections.

statement: Let m be the minimum of connections[i][2] over all 0 <= i < len(connections). Whenever the function returns a result r, if r != -1 then r >= (n - 1) * m.
preconditions: n and connections satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4; 1 <= len(connections) <= 10^4; for every i with 0 <= i < len(connections), len(connections[i]) = 3, 1 <= connections[i][0] <= n, 1 <= connections[i][1] <= n, connections[i][0] != connections[i][1], and 0 <= connections[i][2] <= 10^5.

statement: Let M be the maximum of connections[i][2] over all 0 <= i < len(connections). Whenever the function returns a result r, if r != -1 then r <= (n - 1) * M.
preconditions: n and connections satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4; 1 <= len(connections) <= 10^4; for every i with 0 <= i < len(connections), len(connections[i]) = 3, 1 <= connections[i][0] <= n, 1 <= connections[i][1] <= n, connections[i][0] != connections[i][1], and 0 <= connections[i][2] <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = sum over i from 0 to len(connections)-1 of connections[i][2].
preconditions: n and connections satisfy the problem constraints, and additionally len(connections) = n - 1 and the graph using all given connections connects all cities in {1,...,n}.

statement: Whenever both calls return results r and r_prime, either r = -1 and r_prime = -1, or r != -1, r_prime != -1, and r <= r_prime.
preconditions: Both (n, connections) and (n, connections_prime) satisfy the problem constraints. They have the same length, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(connections): connections_prime[i][0] = connections[i][0], connections_prime[i][1] = connections[i][1], and connections[i][2] <= connections_prime[i][2].
